title: Modi opens 19.7 km Nitish Setu over the Ganga, launches ₹34,470 crore Bihar projects
dek: At a Vaishali rally marking a year of the NDA's current term, the Prime Minister praised Nitish Kumar and Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary. The RJD's Tejashwi Yadav said some works were already open.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday opened a 19.7 km, six-lane bridge over the Ganga between Patna and Vaishali, named Nitish Setu after former chief minister Nitish Kumar, and launched projects that the government valued at about ₹34,470 crore, at a rally marking one year of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government's current term in Bihar.

At the rally in Vaishali, Mr Modi praised Mr Kumar and his successor. "Under the leadership of respected Nitish ji, Bihar found a new assurance in the form of good governance," he said, according to reports. "Now, with his blessings, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and his entire team are carrying forward this mission."

## What was launched

The bridge links Kachchi Dargah in Patna district with Bidupur in Vaishali and cost about ₹4,280 crore, according to the government. It is expected to take traffic off the two older Ganga crossings at Patna, Mahatma Gandhi Setu and JP Setu, and to shorten journeys between north and south Bihar.

Projects worth more than ₹15,600 crore were inaugurated or dedicated, including road projects, the six-lane Aurangabad-Chordaha highway, the 660 MW second unit of the Buxar thermal power project, and power transmission, irrigation, education, health and urban works. Foundation stones were laid for projects worth about ₹14,450 crore, among them the four-laning of the Sahebganj-Areraj-Bettiah section of NH-139W, the power evacuation system for the planned Pirpainti thermal power project, and urban water supply and sewerage schemes.

Mr Modi also flagged off 100 electric buses under the PM-eBus scheme, and more than 26,900 beneficiaries of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban received the keys to their houses.

## The political message

Mr Modi used the rally to contrast Bihar's present with the years before 2005, when the NDA first came to power in the state. He said that headlines about Bihar were once about scams and crime and were now about investment, according to reports. He listed investment agreements worth more than ₹2 lakh crore signed in the past year, work on a ₹6,000 crore steel project in Gayaji, a new incentive policy to revive closed sugar mills and plans for 11,000 irrigation tube wells.

He also attacked the Congress over its old "Garibi Hatao" (remove poverty) slogan, saying his government had lifted 50 crore people out of poverty in 12 years, according to reports.

Tejashwi Yadav of the opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal questioned the launch, saying that some of the infrastructure being inaugurated had already been opened months ago, according to reports.

## Background

The NDA, led by the Bharatiya Janata Party and Mr Kumar's Janata Dal (United), returned to power in the Bihar Assembly election in November 2025. Mr Choudhary of the BJP has since taken over as chief minister. Naming the new bridge after Mr Kumar, who led Bihar for most of the past two decades, was described by Mr Modi as the people of Bihar's tribute to his service.

The Vaishali visit came the same day Mr Modi addressed the platinum jubilee of IIT Kharagpur in West Bengal.

## What happens next

The bridge is open to traffic. Several of the projects whose foundation stones were laid on Saturday, including the NH-139W widening and the Pirpainti power evacuation system, have no completion dates in the government's announcement.
